_comment: What a kill is worth, and what gold buys. Every number in the loot layer
lives here; game/loot.py and game/shop.py hold the arithmetic and none of
the values.
IMPORTANT, and unlike the rest of data/: these numbers are a first pass and
have not been measured against a real run. Everything in entities.json and
weapons.json was measured, and several of those numbers were reverted when
the measurement disagreed with the guess. Nothing here has been through
that yet. Treat a price as an opening bid.
Turning the whole system off is two edits: gold.base to 0 and item_chance
to 0. Nothing then drops, the shop can never be afforded, and the code goes
quiet without being removed.
gold = base * monster_level * (1 + floor_step * (floor - 1)), rolled
within +/- variance and never rounding below 1.
Two multipliers rather than one, because they answer different questions.
monster_level is 'was that worth fighting' -- a sovereign pays eight times
a rat wherever they stand. floor_step is 'how deep are you' -- at 0.15 the
twentieth floor pays 3.85x the first, so the same rat is worth more down
there without a rat ever becoming interesting.
A rat on floor 1 pays 3. A sovereign on floor 20 pays about 92.

_drop_comment: item_chance is per kill, on top of the gold, which always drops. A quarter
is often enough that a stage reliably produces a few and rare enough that
the drop itself is the event, before the rarity roll has said anything.
scatter is how far, in pixels, a drop lands from the body -- so a coin and
the valuable beside it are two things rather than one pile. A drop can
scatter into a wall and become unwalkable; that is what the sweep on stage
clear is for, and it means the worst case is collecting it late rather than
_rarity_comment: Weights are relative, not percentages -- they are summed and rolled
against, so adding a tier does not mean rebalancing the others to 100.
As written: common 60%, uncommon 25%, rare 10%, epic 4%, legendary 1%.
'worth' multiplies the same gold figure the kill already produced, so a
rarity is worth more on a deep floor and off a big monster for free. A
legendary off a sovereign on floor 20 is around 1500 gold, which is meant
to be a run-changing amount -- roughly ten stages of ordinary income.
The weights are flat across floors, deliberately. Depth already pays more
through the gold formula, and tilting the rarities as well is two dials
doing one job. If loot starts feeling samey deep in a run, that is the
moment to add a depth term here -- not before.

_comment: limit 0 means no limit. The two permanent goods are capped because they
compound: four Tonics is +24 health back after every remaining stage, and
three Charms is +75% on everything that drops afterwards. Without a cap
the correct play is to buy nothing but Charms early, which is a strategy
the shop should not have.
'amount' means whatever the good does with it -- health for the Poultice,
heal-per-stage for the Tonic, percentage points of gold find for the
Charm. game/shop.py decides which; this decides how much.
THESE PRICES ARE SET AGAINST A MEASUREMENT, unlike the drop numbers above.
A full run banks about 4,700 gold with a bot that never detours for a
pickup, rising from ~33 on floor 1 to ~400-550 on the late floors. The
first draft priced the shop at 45/120/150, which maxed every permanent
good for 930 -- about a fifth of one run, bought out by roughly stage 5,
after which there was nothing left to decide. At 260 and 340 the two
permanents cost 2,060 to max, a little under half a run, and the first
Tonic is out of reach until about floor 4.
What is still NOT measured: whether any of it is worth buying. Nothing
plays this game with a purse -- autoplay never spends -- so the prices are
measured against income and against nothing else.
